title: Maximum Value of K Coins From Piles
summary: Given n piles of coins, where each pile is represented by a list of integers indicating the values of the coins from the top to the bottom, and a positive integer k, determine the maximum total value of k coins that can be selected by picking exactly one coin from any pile in an optimal manner.
statement: Given n piles of coins, where each pile is represented by a list of integers indicating the values of the coins from the top to the bottom, and a positive integer k, determine the maximum total value of k coins that can be selected by picking exactly one coin from any pile in an optimal manner.
constraints: Coins in each pile are ordered from top to bottom.
Taking x coins from a pile requires taking exactly its first x values.
Take exactly k coins across all piles and maximize their total value.
hints: A state needs only how many coins have been taken after processing some piles.
Precompute each pile’s prefix values and try every feasible take count from that pile.
Carry dp[used], update dp[used+take] with prior value plus prefix[take], and preserve take zero.
Every legal selection chooses one prefix length per pile; the transitions enumerate these choices and retain the best total for each exact count.
editorial: Every legal selection chooses one prefix length per pile; the transitions enumerate these choices and retain the best total for each exact count.

tests.explanation: Taking the first two coins from the first pile gives 101, better than every other valid choice.
Taking the entire final pile yields 706 and is better than taking one coin from each of the six hundred-value piles.
